headline: Ishraque to announce resignation as State Minister for Liberation War Affairs today
summary: Ishraque Hossain will make a final announcement at 2 PM at the National Press Club, following a Facebook post this morning. He will also address journalists.
details: Ishraque Hossain has announced his intention to resign from his position as the State Minister for Liberation War Affairs. He shared this information in a verified Facebook post on Monday morning, shortly after 8:30 AM.
In his post, Ishraque stated that he would make a final declaration of his resignation at 2 PM today at the National Press Club. He is also scheduled to meet with journalists there.
caption:
State Minister Ishraque Hossain is set to announce his resignation from the Ministry of Liberation War Affairs today. He revealed his decision via a Facebook post.

Ishraque Hossain has announced his intention to resign from his position as the State Minister for Liberation War Affairs. He shared this information in a verified Facebook post on Monday morning, shortly after 8:30 AM.

In his post, Ishraque stated that he would make a final declaration of his resignation at 2 PM today at the National Press Club. He is also scheduled to meet with journalists there.

headline_marked: Jobs sold for 20 lakh: [[Question leaks and 'center-contracts' plague government hiring]]
headline: Jobs sold for 20 lakh: Question leaks and 'center-contracts' plague government hiring
summary: From the Department of Youth Development to primary school teachers, systemic corruption and question leaks are shattering the dreams of millions of job seekers.
details: A recruitment exam for Assistant Upazila Youth Development Officers was postponed just two minutes before the start after question papers leaked on social media. Over 318,000 candidates had applied for 242 vacancies, leaving thousands of devastated job seekers in Dhaka.

An SRB investigation revealed a sophisticated racket using fake WhatsApp IDs to distribute answers. Bribes ranged from 8 to 10 lakh BDT for third-class positions and 15 to 20 lakh BDT for second-class roles, with five government employees among seven arrested.

Beyond leaks, 'center-contracts' have emerged as a new threat. This involves collusion between dishonest officials and exam centers to provide specific candidates with special advantages, including sending solutions via digital devices during the exam.

Similar irregularities were reported during the recent primary school assistant teacher recruitment process. In Nilphamari, candidates protested after answers were allegedly supplied from outside and special favors were granted in specific rooms.

The scale of the corruption is exemplified by Syed Abed Ali, a former PSC driver who ran a leak network for years. Despite multiple cases and charge sheets, a lack of judicial progress has allowed such rackets to persist.

Experts, including DU Professor Tanjim Uddin Khan, blame institutional dishonesty and political appointments in exam committees. He argues that honesty and skill should be the only criteria for these roles, rather than political loyalty.
caption:
Jobs sold for up to 20 lakh BDT. Question leaks and 'center-contracts' are turning government recruitment into a business of bribes.

A recruitment exam for Assistant Upazila Youth Development Officers was postponed just two minutes before the start after question papers leaked on social media. Over 318,000 candidates had applied for 242 vacancies, leaving thousands of devastated job seekers in Dhaka.

An SRB investigation revealed a sophisticated racket using fake WhatsApp IDs to distribute answers. Bribes ranged from 8 to 10 lakh BDT for third-class positions and 15 to 20 lakh BDT for second-class roles, with five government employees among seven arrested.

Beyond leaks, 'center-contracts' have emerged as a new threat. This involves collusion between dishonest officials and exam centers to provide specific candidates with special advantages, including sending solutions via digital devices during the exam.

Similar irregularities were reported during the recent primary school assistant teacher recruitment process. In Nilphamari, candidates protested after answers were allegedly supplied from outside and special favors were granted in specific rooms.

The scale of the corruption is exemplified by Syed Abed Ali, a former PSC driver who ran a leak network for years. Despite multiple cases and charge sheets, a lack of judicial progress has allowed such rackets to persist.

Experts, including DU Professor Tanjim Uddin Khan, blame institutional dishonesty and political appointments in exam committees. He argues that honesty and skill should be the only criteria for these roles, rather than political loyalty.
